title: Phase 2 pivot
objective: Strengthen planetary and mission defense without seriously destabilizing attack pressure or delaying early attacks.

prior_phase.outstanding_runs: Completed all three bilateral runs and all six faction-isolated comparisons.
prior_phase.causal_check: In every seed, changing Empire alone reproduced the full bilateral report; changing Alliance alone reproduced the full comparison report, excluding only OutputPath. The third Empire decline therefore occurs under its own changed policy against an unchanged opposing policy. Its complete downstream cause is not established.
prior_phase.officer_trial: Held out the unsupported-command reassignment trial. In the matched turn-1000 to turn-1100 continuation, the displaced admiral remained in transit while another officer took command, and the target fleet departed six turns later than the control.

verification.clean_replay: The hook-free production build exactly reproduced the successful 1000-turn candidate report, excluding only OutputPath.
verification.build_all: Formatting, compilation, 38 analyzer tests, and 9 architecture tests passed. The full command stopped on the same pre-existing RCS1163 and RCS1213 lint errors. The repository is not fully green.

phase_2_work: Trace defense demand, placement, producer allocation, maintenance reservations, and execution through their existing owners.
Measure shields, defensive starfighters, garrisons, hostile mission outcomes, officer losses, world losses, and idle manufacturing separately for each faction and seed.
Measure first attack timing, ground assaults, bombardments, offensive departures, fleet losses, production, research, and economy alongside defense.
Investigate fewer fleet commitments as an optional tuning lever, not an assumed solution.
Trace attack declines and use faction-isolated comparisons before attributing them to stronger opposition.
Keep incremental commits only for improvements supported by concrete gameplay evidence.
constraints: Do not restore manufacturing forecasting, advanced preplanning, or external optimization dependencies.
Keep normal one-unit production orders and the existing proposal, scoring, selection, and command architecture.
Verify loaded Unity assemblies before every simulation; save and reload through the existing simulation runner.
Keep experiment controls and diagnostic hooks outside production commits.
Preserve unrelated working-tree edits and do not push or deploy without authorization.
